id_and_class.theory_title: Gray’s Brain-Built World-Model: Qualia, Comparators, Late-Error Detection
id_and_class.summary: Jeffrey Gray argues that phenomenal consciousness is a slow, brain-built multimodal display of the organism and its world, produced by unconscious systems and consulted by other unconscious systems. It arrives too late to steer most behavior, so its job is late error detection: a stable model against which a comparator checks outcomes against predictions. Gray openly denied that this explains why any of it is felt.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Display for Late Error Detection

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a brain-constructed simulated world, and qualia are the felt properties of that construction, presented as a unified model for comparison against prediction.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Gray rejected dualism and held experience to be generated by brain processes, but denied that identifying neural correlates or functions explains why those processes are felt.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Unspecified emergence from brain processes; Gray left the explanatory gap open.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Intentionality, binding and behavioral control are all achieved unconsciously, so Gray set them aside as not the hard part. Features are bound into objects before awareness, and a duck-rabbit figure arrives already interpreted.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are the sole genuine explanandum. Percepts are signals that need not resemble what they signal, and synesthesia shows that qualia can come apart from function, which Gray took to refute reductive functionalism.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Unconscious neural systems, the septo-hippocampal comparator, a brain-built multimodal display, and qualia as real features of experience.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Experimental psychology, neuropsychology, timing studies and functional imaging of synesthetes.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Unconscious perceptual and action-control systems produce outputs that are presented together in one conscious model; a comparator in the septo-hippocampal system checks that model against predictions.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (qualia) and the function of conscious perception; intentionality and binding are treated as unconscious achievements.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Late error detection: the conscious display gives a comparator a stable, integrated, cross-modal model in which mismatches between outcome and prediction show up, so unconscious servomechanisms can be adjusted next time.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: A visual percept takes roughly a quarter-second to form, so consciousness lags behind the fast systems that control action.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Constructed by distributed unconscious systems; the comparator relies on the septo-hippocampal system, with the medial septum regulating hippocampal theta rhythm. Visual qualia depend on the ventral stream, visually guided action on the dorsal stream.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Causal only in an attenuated sense: like a sketch that downstream systems consult, the display cannot initiate or inhibit action. Gray credits it with late error detection, smoothing jerky input, and the shared consensus behind language and science.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Binding happens unconsciously, before awareness; consciousness presents the already bound result as one multimodal model.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The hippocampus predicts what comes next and the comparator flags mismatch with incoming signals. Pain, which typically arrives after the hand has withdrawn, illustrates the display's role in making repetition less likely.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Because organisms err, they need a way to detect errors after the fact, and that requires a stable model of the environment.
core_claims_and_evidence: Conscious percepts form too slowly to control fast actions such as returning a tennis serve, and the dorsal action stream is dissociable from the ventral stream that yields visual qualia.
In colored-hearing synesthesia, spoken words activate color area V4 without earlier visual-pathway involvement.
The alien color effect, where synesthetic color opposes the real color, separates qualia from function.
Gray rejected Penrose-Hameroff quantum proposals because wave-function collapse does not explain why one quale rather than another occurs.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical: experimental psychology, neuropsychology and neuroimaging, plus philosophical argument against functionalism.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Timing studies of visual perception, dorsal-ventral stream dissociations, and fMRI of synesthetes (V4 activation by spoken words; the alien color effect).
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The benefits Gray credits to consciousness would accrue equally to an unconscious mechanism doing the same operations. Gray also held some non-linguistic animals to be conscious, though they lack the distinctive functions he names. Kriegel and Biggs note that a display seems to need an audience, bringing back a homunculus.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Gray explicitly denied solving the hard problem; he claimed only to have narrowed it by showing what consciousness does and what it is not.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: A naturalistic, anti-dualist account that rejects reductive functionalism while leaving the nature of qualia unexplained, which makes its final ontology open.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Gray's synesthesia argument holds that qualia are not fixed by function, so reproducing a brain's functions in a machine would not guarantee experience.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since Gray rejected dualism and takes experience to be constructed by the brain, it ends with the brain.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Consciousness is explained by an adaptive biological function.

virtual_immortality.rationale: If qualia do not follow from function, a functional simulation of a person would not reliably carry their experience.
